text:
maria: Hey — trying to use @redwood/inference-js inside Next.js middleware (Edge runtime) and it's blowing up during build with "crypto not found" and syntax errors. Anyone seen this?

sam: Yup. The SDK ships a Node-targeted bundle by default so Vercel/swc picks up requires like `crypto`, `stream`, etc. Edge runtime can't handle those.

maria: Ugh. Error log: `Error: Can't resolve 'crypto'` and then `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` from a dependency.

kai: Two quick options: 1) use the published edge/browser build entrypoint (we added `/edge` and `/browser` exports), 2) dynamic import inside the middleware so bundler can tree-shake server-only bits.

ashley: Example we used in a customer PoC: 
```ts
// middleware.ts
export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'

export default async function middleware(req: NextRequest) {
  // dynamic import the ESM edge-friendly bundle at runtime
  const mod = await import('@redwood/inference-js/edge')
  const client = mod.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RI_KEY })
  const out = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hello from middleware' })
  return new NextResponse(out.text)
}
```

sam: Also, if you only have the CJS build available, wrap the import in a try/catch and fallback to a lightweight fetch wrapper to the hosted API. That avoids bundling node-only deps.

maria: Types are annoying too — `createClient` expects `Request` but Next's middleware gives `NextRequest`. Any neat typings workarounds?

kai: For now we cast: `const r = req as unknown as Request` when forwarding the incoming headers/body. We're planning a small patch to add `types/edge.d.ts` that exports overloads for Next/Cloudflare/Workers.

ashley: FYI we added a new export map in the SDK package.json so Node consumers get `exports.node` and edge consumers get `exports.edge`. That should unblock most cases once you use `@redwood/inference-js/edge`.

maria: Are there any SWC bundler quirks I should watch out for?

sam: Yes — avoid importing optional dev-only modules at top-level. Vercel's bundler will still try to resolve them. Use conditional/dynamic import. Also ensure package.json `exports` doesn't list server-only files under the top-level path.

maria: Cool. I tried the dynamic import trick and build proceeds further but runtime fails with `TypeError: fetch is not a function` inside the SDK (it was using a small node fetch shim).

ashley: Right — edge runtime provides a global `fetch` but the SDK falls back to `node-fetch` in some builds. The edge build should assume global fetch. If you accidentally pulled the node build, you'll hit that.

kai: Quick dev checklist: 
- import from `@redwood/inference-js/edge` not root
- dynamic import in middleware if you see CJS errors
- cast `NextRequest` -> `Request` for types or wait for `edge.d.ts`
- ensure no top-level `fs`/`crypto` imports in your app code path

maria: Saved my day, thanks. Is there an open issue/PR we can track for adding better DX?

sam: Yep — PR #842 in mono repo adds `edge` export and updates the TS types for Next/Cloudflare. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 (will land tomorrow).
